subject: general
question: If sqrt {3} tanA = 3 sinA , find the value of (2sqrt{3}cosecA times tanA).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: √3 tanA = 3 sinA

⇒ √3 (sinA/cosA) = 3 sinA

⇒ cosA = √3/3 = 1/√3

Value required: 2√3 cosecA × tanA = 2√3 (1/sinA) × (sinA/cosA) = 2√3/cosA

⇒ 2√3 ÷ (1/√3) = 2√3 × √3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82659d52c19fef2820119a60f5b19c1fb5ab2f0d80ee5a398eb9d6300b910c47.png] 

**Given:** √3 tanA = 3 sinA

**Formula Used:** tanA = sinA/cosA, cosecA = 1/sinA

⇒ √3 (sinA/cosA) = 3 sinA

⇒ 1/cosA = 3/√3

⇒ cosA = √3/3 = 1/√3

⇒ Base (B) = 1, Hypotenuse (H) = √3

⇒ Perpendicular (P) = √(H² − B²) = √(3 − 1) = √2

⇒ Target expression = 2√3 cosecA × tanA

⇒ Target expression = 2√3 × (H/P) × (P/B) = 2√3 × (H/B)

⇒ Target expression = 2√3 × (√3/1)

⇒ 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: tanA = sinA/cosA, cotA = cosA/sinA, and sin²A + cos²A = 1.

Reciprocal Ratios

cosecA = 1/sinA, secA = 1/cosA, and cotA = 1/tanA.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, P² + B² = H² where P is perpendicular, B is base, and H is hypotenuse.</p
